production.note: US model years. First: the 2018 press kit says 'A limited number of 2017 RS 3 models will be produced. These will be the first vehicles arriving in the US' (a token early run, counted). Last: Audi of America's April 2020 release covers 'the 2020 Audi RS 3 Nardo edition' (audi-us-2020-rs3-nardo); J.D. Power's model-year list for the RS 3 runs 2017-2020 then 2022 onward (jdpower-rs3-model-years), the 2022 car being the next generation.

body.note: 'All-new 2018 RS 3 sedan'; only the sedan was sold in the US.

aspiration.note: TFSI turbocharged five-cylinder; a single turbocharger.

drivetrain.note: 'Seven-speed S tronic dual-clutch automatic transmission and quattro'

transmission.note: 'Seven-speed S tronic dual-clutch automatic transmission' (S tronic is a DCT). No manual.

powerHp.note: Quote: "400 @ 5,850-7,000" (horsepower row). 400 hp applied to model years 2017-2018; for 2019-2020 Audi of America rated the car at 394 hp ('producing 394 horsepower and 354 lb-ft of torque', audi-us-2020-rs3-nardo). The two ratings each cover two model years, so the launch rating is used.

weightLb.note: Sedan, 7-speed S tronic (the only configuration), 2018 model year. Quote: "3,593 (1630 kg)" (curb weight row of the technical specifications; no estimate label). Cars.com and KBB list the same 3,593 lb for 2017. The 2018 press kit is the earliest opened source with a manufacturer weight, so 2018 is the reference year.

sources.publisher: Audi of America (press kit hosted by AudiWorld)
